raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not like to take big risks. On these 2 mu I will still do wheat and then maize, same as before. This rotation feeds the family first and still gives some cash. I watch what the farmers around me do. If I change too much and it goes wrong, on such a small piece of land I have no room to make it back. Wheat I will sow in early October after I clean the field, using a common local improved seed that people nearby use. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, not too little because wheat cannot look weak over winter, but not too much because fertilizer costs money. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing, I will topdress once more. Since I have well water, I will irrigate about three times for wheat if rainfall is not enough: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once around jointing, and once around filling. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize quickly, within a few days, because the window is short. For maize I will use hybrid seed like my neighbors do. I will put some fertilizer at planting and one topdress around the big bell stage. Maize usually needs less water than wheat here, so if rain is normal I will irrigate once or twice. I will not spend much on pesticide unless I really see weeds or insects. On 2 mu, every yuan matters, so I keep the plan steady and practical.
